@Bitcast_network #sn93 had a bottleneck: the subnet owner was the only one that could bring in new customers to the subnet.  Miners could easily meet brief criteria- but the subnet owner had to manually setup campaigns with customers.  As a miner, this bottleneck was the clearest issue/unlock- miners could satisfy demand, but the subnet owner could only bring in so much demand manually by themselves.

They're now moving to a mechanism that allows their customers to:

1. Build their own access to the subnet (bypassing the bottleneck)
2. BUY their alpha in order to GAIN ACCESS to content creators (miners)

Bitcast was already permissionless for miners (content creators), but NOW it's becoming permissionless for their customers.

This is really shaping up to be a bittensor subnet that realizes the dream of creating a permissionless, commodity flywheel.

Insane!!

tweets.text:
I had trouble understanding @green_compute_ Bittensor #sn110 so I've broken it down simply, and included what I learned from the subnet owner as far as the investibility of the subnet:

Cows poop ⤵ 
Poop goes into digester ⤵ 
Bacteria turn it into methane ⤵ 
Methane burns in generator ⤵ 
Generator makes electricity ⤵ 
Electricity powers the GPUs

Essentially turning cow poop into electricity and then using that electricity to power GPUs.  Those GPUs are rented-out by @green_compute_ .  This is a pretty compelling case, and this sort of [poop into GPUs] is a functional model being used by other companies as well- I had no idea this existed.

I'm actually very excited to see if this can work as a long-term subnet, I think it CAN, but it's tricky and requires transparency.  It would run more like a traditional business than a regular decentralized permissionless business, which I think can run very well on bittensor.

I asked the subnet owner about their locks/burns/revenue plans, you can see the convo in the screenshots.

Q: Are there lock/burn plans?  Answer: Mebe, TBD.

Q: What is going on with the subnet owner wallet transfers?  Answer: DSV is involved here, not sure the exact arrangement.

Q: What's happening with buybacks?  Answer: Buybacks are set at 10% of revenues generated from compute contracts.

More thoughts:

1. There is currently 1 miner UID on the subnet receiving emissions.  I think there's no secret that miners are permissioned on the subnet, which makes me wonder how bittensor adds value here.

2. It's still early days and not clear to me that value will be driven back into the alpha token yet.  I wish Green Compute the best and I hope that we can report some value being driven into the alpha  token via burns/locks in the future.

I actually think that centralized companies can/should run on bittensor, as it's just more transparent than traditional businesses.  We get to ask these sorts of questions and deeply understand facts about what the company is doing and how they might drive value to their token.
